Director Operations
Lane Cove is Australia’s most liveable community, named so in the 2025 Australian Liveability Census: a Lower North Shore community of close to 43,000 people, around ten kilometres from the CBD, with distinctive village neighbourhoods, a strong sense of community and a natural environment its residents value highly. Council’s infrastructure, facilities and open spaces are central to that quality of life, and the community rightly expects them to be well planned, well maintained and well managed.

The Director Operations leads that portfolio at the executive table. This is an appointment for an accomplished and contemporary leader who can hold strategy and delivery in the same hand: setting the long-term direction for Council’s assets and services, while ensuring the work on the ground is safe, efficient and visibly delivered for the community.

The Role
Reporting to the General Manager as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Director Operations provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of the Operations Directorate. The portfolio is broad: facilities and asset management, open space, sport and recreation facilities, civic services, traffic and transport, capital project delivery and civil works, and Council’s commercial operations, including its property portfolio. You will lead five direct reports and carry accountability for Council’s long-term asset management planning, the delivery of its capital program and the sustainable use of its resources.

Beyond the portfolio, the role contributes to the leadership of the whole organisation: working transparently with the elected Council on strategy and policy, shaping medium to long-term business plans aligned with the Community Strategic Plan, championing customer-centricity and continuous improvement, and modelling a culture in which safety and wellbeing sit at the forefront of everything the Directorate does.

You are an experienced executive with a record of leading and developing senior leadership teams, ideally in complex public sector environments. You bring demonstrated success in the delivery of capital and civil infrastructure projects, technical depth across areas such as engineering, civil works, architecture or project management, and the commercial discipline to manage finance, people, assets and risk with rigour. Tertiary qualifications in a relevant discipline are essential; local or state government experience and postgraduate study are desirable.

Just as important is how you lead. The General Manager is seeking a leader who is passionate about local government and not afraid to challenge the status quo; who builds trust, brings people together and creates an environment where people perform at their best. You are politically astute, comfortable navigating complexity and leading through change, and able to turn strategy into practical, visible outcomes for the community.

Why This Role
Lane Cove offers a rare combination: a council of a scale where a Director’s influence is direct and visible, an engaged community that values what Council delivers, and a leadership team that prizes collaboration, integrity, professionalism and a willingness to have a go. For a leader who wants to shape the places and services that matter to a community, and see the results of that work, this is a defining appointment. job.title: Senior Planner
job.description:
Queenstown Airport is entering a significant period of infrastructure development and planning change. With a $65 million airfield programme under construction and a major terminal expansion progressing, it is seeking a Senior Planner to help guide the statutory pathways that will enable its future development.
Capstone Recruitment is partnering with Queenstown Airport Corporation (QAC) to appoint a newly created Senior Planner. QAC owns and operates Queenstown Airport and runs day to day operations at Wānaka Airport on behalf of Queenstown Lakes District Council. It is New Zealand's fourth busiest airport, with 2.82 million passenger movements in the year to 30 June 2026, more than a million of them international for the first time.


About the role
A standalone position reporting to the Head of Planning & Sustainability, this is QAC's lead statutory planning role. You will own the consenting strategy behind the airport's infrastructure programme, hold its designations, and represent QAC in hearings, mediation and policy processes as planning legislation and the district plan evolve. You will set the direction and direct external specialists rather than produce every technical report yourself, and as the first person in the role, you will have a real say in what it becomes.


What you will do
  • Set the consenting strategy across the infrastructure programme, choosing the statutory pathway for each project rather than reacting to it
  • Prepare and lodge resource consents, Notices of Requirement and outline plans, and hold QAC's designations
  • Represent QAC at hearings, mediation and expert conferencing, and in the Environment Court where required
  • Protect the airport's ability to operate as Queenstown develops around it, including the reverse sensitivity risk that noise creates
  • Lead QAC's submissions on new planning legislation, national planning standards and the district plan review
  • Form QAC's position on third party proposals that could affect airport operations or safeguarding
  • Brief and direct external planning, legal and technical advisers, and hold them to their advice
  • Give project managers and the executive a clear read on planning risk early enough to act on it

What we are looking for
  • Around eight to ten years in statutory planning, resource management, infrastructure or environmental planning
  • Advanced command of New Zealand resource management legislation. A planning related qualification is preferred
  • Complex consents and designations taken end to end, including evidence you have written and then defended
  • Experience in a hearing room, in mediation and across the table from a council
  • A planner who starts from how an outcome can be achieved rather than why it cannot
  • Comfort in a small team where you own your area outright and the shape of the work will keep changing
  • Experience in aviation, transport, ports, utilities, transmission or other significant infrastructure is an advantage, though not essential
  • A genuine intention to be based in Queenstown
